reply.text:
Pikes Peak is a big day, and I'd like to know what your legs and your program look like before I answer. Let me pull up your program status and recent workouts. Nothing is logged for your program or your last week of workouts, so I can't see what legs you'd be taking into tomorrow. Here is my general take. A long hike at altitude is a lot of work for the quads and calves, and it is a lot of work for the lungs and the whole body, so a heavy leg session the day before will leave you stiff and flat on the trail. If today's session is a heavy squat or deadlift day, I'd skip it or cut it to light, easy work with plenty of rest between sets. If it's a light day, a short easy session is fine.

Tell me what you had planned for legs today, and I'll give you a straighter answer. And if you'd like, I can also walk you through getting ready for the altitude itself.
